#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=TravailGPU
#flux: -t 20:00:00
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 10

# The Slurm QoS directive is translated to the Flux queue directive.
#flux: -q qos_gpu-t3

# The Slurm output/error directives are combined into a single output file.
# The '%j' variable is replaced with Flux's '{job.id}'.
#flux: -o TravailGPU{job.id}.out

# The following Slurm directive for account was not translated as it is not a standard Flux option.
# It must be filled in by the user or is handled by site-specific policies.
# #SBATCH -A yqs@v100

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU and will NOT be guaranteed a 'v100-32g' node type.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
# #SBATCH -C v100-32g

# The Slurm hint 'nomultithread' is a scheduler-level configuration and cannot be set with a simple Flux directive.
# The request for 10 CPUs on a single task implies that the user wants to control thread placement manually or via
# environment variables like OMP_NUM_THREADS. Performance may differ if the underlying system has hyperthreading enabled.
# #SBATCH --hint=nomultithread

module purge # nettoyer les modules herites par defaut
module load pytorch-gpu/py3/1.10.1 # charger les modules

# The python command is run directly, as this is a single-task job.
# The allocated resources (10 CPUs) are available to this process.
python -u train_gym.py #OVERRIDE IN CONFIG
#python -u train_dm_custom.py #upright # executer son script

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) and the specific node type (`-C v100-32g`). While the translated script is syntactically valid, it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU (unless the 'qos_gpu-t3' queue automatically provides one), and will almost certainly fail at runtime when the `pytorch-gpu` module attempts to access a device.

The Slurm hint '--hint=nomultithread' was not translated. If the underlying system has hyperthreading enabled, the 10 allocated CPUs may correspond to logical cores on fewer than 10 physical cores. This could lead to performance degradation compared to the original Slurm job, which would have enforced placement on 10 distinct physical cores.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -A yqs@v100
#SBATCH --job-name=TravailGPU # nom du job
#SBATCH -C v100-32g # reserver des GPU 16 Go seulement
#SBATCH --qos=qos_gpu-t3 # QoS
#SBATCH --output=TravailGPU%j.out # fichier de sortie (%j = job ID)
#SBATCH --error=TravailGPU%j.err # fichier d’erreur (%j = job ID)
#SBATCH --nodes=1 # reserver 1 nœud
#SBATCH --ntasks=1 # reserver 4 taches (ou processus MPI)
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1 # reserver 4 GPU
##SBATCH --partition=gpu_p4
##SBATCH --cpus-per-task=6 #server 10 CPU par tache (et memoire associee)
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=10 #server 10 CPU par tache (et memoire associee)
#SBATCH --hint=nomultithread # desactiver l’hyperthreading
#SBATCH --time=20:00:00

module purge # nettoyer les modules herites par defaut
module load pytorch-gpu/py3/1.10.1 # charger les modules
srun python -u train_gym.py #OVERRIDE IN CONFIG
#srun python -u train_dm_custom.py #upright # executer son script
